question: Who conducted an X-ray spectroscopic study of a large number of elements and showed that the frequency of X-rays emitted by an element is related to the atomic number, Z, rather than the atomic mass?
solution:
The correct option is __**Henry Moseley**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1913 AD, the English scientist** Henry Moseley **demonstrated, with the help of experiments done using an X-ray tube, that the **atomic number (Z) of an element corresponds to the positive charge on the nucleus or the number of the protons in the nucleus of the atom of that element**.
 
• This revealed that the atomic number is a more fundamental property of an element than its atomic mass.
 
• Henry Moseley observed **regularities in the characteristic** X-ray spectra of the elements. A plot frequency of X-ray emitted against **atomic number gave a straight line and the plot of the frequency of X-rays emitted vs atomic mass was not a straight line**.
 
• Based on the above experiments he proposed that the physical and chemical properties of the elements are periodic functions of their atomic number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A German chemist, **Julius Lothar Meyer** 1869, was looking at the physical properties of elements along with their valence states. He made a table that contained a preliminary tabulation of 28 elements. The table showed how the integral valence changed as the atomic weight of elements increase
 
• On 17 February 1869, **Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev** jotted down the symbols for the chemical elements, putting them in order according to their atomic weights and inventing the periodic table. He wrote down the sequence in such a way that they ended up grouped on the page according to known regularities or ‘periodicities’ of behaviour. It was perhaps the greatest breakthrough in the history of chemistry
 
• In 1829** Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner** discovered the **existence of families of elements with similar chemical** properties. Because there always seemed to be three elements in these families, he called them triads.
